the customer has picked a number of stars

the pointer is over a star

meaning.name: Give feedback
meaning.purpose: The customer ends with their feedback received, and thanked for it.
meaning.steps: 1. The customer opens the feedback page from a request, or by scanning the printed QR code. SC3, SC4, SC1, R13, R16 2. They pick 1 to 5 stars, write what they want to say, or both, with no account. SC1, R1, R6 3. If they want a reply, they leave an email address. SC1, R5 4. If the business may publish their words, they tick the permission. SC1, R9 5. They press Send. With everything empty, the page says there is nothing to send. SC1, R1 6. An address that does not look right is refused, and their words stay. SC1, R5 7. If the feedback cannot be kept, the page says it was not received, and their words stay to send again. SC1, R1 8. The website keeps it with the date and time, and says thank you. SC1, R2 9. Feedback rated 1 or 2 stars is emailed to every member of staff. SC10, R11

meaning.name: Stop feedback requests
meaning.purpose: The customer ends with no more requests, and is still able to give feedback.
meaning.steps: 1. The customer selects the Stop link in a request. SC3, SC4, R17 2. The page asks them to confirm, and they press Stop asking me. SC2, R17 3. A link the website did not give says so, and nothing changes. SC2 4. If the opt-out cannot be kept, the page says so and they can press again. SC2, R17 5. The website keeps the opt-out with its date, and says they won't be asked again. SC2, R22 6. They can still give feedback from the link on that page. SC2, SC1, R17

meaning.goes wrong: A request that cannot be delivered does not stop any other customer's request. R13 If the website is down when a request falls due, it sends it once it is back. R21
meaning.name: The request after delivery
meaning.purpose: A customer who has their order is asked for feedback once, and no oftener than once a month.
meaning.steps: 1. The shop platform says an order has been delivered. R13 2. Where no delivery can be known, the website waits until 7 days after the order. R18 3. A customer who opted out is skipped. R17 4. A customer who had a request in the past month is skipped. R14 5. A customer who has an email address is sent the request by email. SC3, R15 6. A customer with only a mobile number is sent it by text message. SC4, R15 7. A customer who cannot be reached is skipped, and nothing else changes. R13
meaning.trigger: an order's delivery becoming known, or 7 days after an order with no delivery known

meaning.name: Read the feedback
meaning.purpose: A member of staff ends having read everything customers have said, and signed out.
meaning.steps: 1. A member of staff opens the staff address and signs in. SC5, R4 2. A wrong password is refused, and repeated failures are blocked for a time. SC5, R4 3. They read the feedback, the newest first, with each date and time. SC6, R3, R2 4. They see each rating, and feedback rated 1 or 2 stars is marked Unhappy. SC6, R6, R10 5. They see the customer's address where one was left, and reply from their own email. SC6, R5 6. They see which feedback may be published, and since when. SC6, R9, R22 7. With nothing yet, the list says so. SC6, R3 8. They sign out. SC6, SC5, R23

meaning.name: Act on an unhappy customer
meaning.purpose: A member of staff hears of an unhappy customer as soon as the feedback arrives, and replies.
meaning.steps: 1. Feedback rated 1 or 2 stars arrives, and every member of staff receives an email holding it. SC10, R11 2. They open the list from the email, signing in first where needed. SC10, SC5, SC6, R4 3. The feedback stands marked Unhappy. SC6, R10 4. They reply from their own email where the customer left an address; with none, they cannot reply. SC6, R5

meaning.name: Remove spam
meaning.purpose: A member of staff ends with the spam gone from the list and from the monthly figures.
meaning.steps: 1. A member of staff finds spam or abuse in the list, and presses Remove. SC6, R12 2. The website asks them to confirm; Keep it leaves everything as it was. SC7, R12 3. They press Remove, and it leaves the list and the monthly figures. SC7, SC6, R12 4. If it cannot be removed, the dialog says so, and the feedback stays. SC7, R12

meaning.name: Check the monthly figures
meaning.purpose: A member of staff reads the month's numbers and sees whether things are better or worse.
meaning.steps: 1. A member of staff signs in and opens the monthly figures. SC5, SC8, R4 2. They read how many pieces of feedback arrived each month. SC8, R8 3. They read each month's average rating; a month with no ratings shows none. SC8, R7 4. They read how many requests went out and how many customers opted out. SC8, R20 5. They read who opted out, and when. SC8, R22

meaning.name: Print the link and QR code
meaning.purpose: A member of staff ends with a link and QR code to print on receipts and in parcels.
meaning.steps: 1. A member of staff signs in and opens Link and QR code. SC5, SC9, R4 2. They copy the link, or save the QR code. SC9, R16 3. They print it on receipts and in parcels, outside the website. R16

meaning.name: Deleting old feedback
meaning.purpose: Feedback, and the email address left with it, goes after 12 months.
meaning.steps: 1. A piece of feedback reaches 12 months old. R19 2. The website deletes it and the email address kept with it. R19 3. Opt-outs stay, so that the customer is never asked again. R19
meaning.trigger: a piece of feedback reaching 12 months old

meaning.if: Too little feedback keeps arriving, and the target is missed.
meaning.mitigation: Check the response rate after the first month, then change the wording or the timing of the requests.
meaning.risk: Requests go out and few customers answer them.

meaning.if: Unhappy customers still leave, and the goals are missed though the number looks good.
meaning.mitigation: One named person reads the feedback on a set day each week.
meaning.risk: Feedback arrives and staff are too busy to read it or respond.

meaning.says: The website's server side is written in Python.
What the website keeps is held in a database. Which database is engineering's to choose.
Orders come from four places: an online shop platform, the business's own online shop, its physical shop, and marketplaces.
The first release may take up to 3 months.

meaning.answers: whoever runs the business's online shop
meaning.question: Which shop platform, order systems and marketplaces does the business use, and can each one say when an order was delivered?
meaning.why: A request goes out on delivery, so the website needs each place to tell it who bought and when it arrived. A sale in the physical shop has no delivery to wait for.

meaning.answers: whoever looks after legal or data protection
meaning.question: May the business use customers' email addresses and mobile numbers to ask for feedback, and what must it do to comply?
meaning.why: Whoever looks after legal or data protection could stop the requests, and what the law requires is not the specification's to assume.

meaning.question: After how many failed sign-ins is someone refused, and for how long?
meaning.why: Repeated failures must be blocked, and the number is for whoever builds it to set.

meaning.question: What is the business's name, and is there a logo?
meaning.why: The screens say [Business name], with a plain mark, until this is known.

meaning.name: Give feedback without an account
meaning.statement: The website shall let anyone who opens it send feedback without signing in.

meaning.says: Given a person with no account, when they open the website, write 'The delivery was late' and send it, then the website says their feedback was received.
Given a person who leaves everything empty, when they send it, then the website says there is nothing to send and keeps nothing.
Given the website cannot keep the feedback, when a person sends it, then the website says it was not received and their words stay on the page to send again.
Given a person who presses Send twice on the same feedback, when both arrive, then one piece of feedback is kept.

meaning.name: Unhappy feedback stands out
meaning.statement: When feedback rated 1 or 2 stars arrives, the website shall mark it in the staff's list.

meaning.says: Given feedback rated 2 stars, when staff open the list, then it is marked.
Given feedback rated 3 stars, when staff open the list, then it is not marked.
Given feedback with no rating, when staff open the list, then it is not marked.

meaning.name: Email staff about an unhappy user
meaning.statement: When feedback rated 1 or 2 stars arrives, the website shall email every member of staff.

meaning.says: Given feedback rated 2 stars, when it arrives, then every member of staff receives one email holding the rating and what was written.
Given feedback rated 3 stars, when it arrives, then no email is sent.
Given feedback with no rating, when it arrives, then no email is sent.
Given the email cannot be sent, when feedback rated 1 star arrives, then the feedback is still kept and marked in the staff's list.

meaning.name: Remove feedback
meaning.statement: When a member of staff removes a piece of feedback, the website shall take it out of the list and the monthly figures.

meaning.says: Given 12 pieces of feedback in March, when staff remove one, then the list no longer shows it and March shows 11.
Given a removed piece of feedback rated 1 star, when staff look at its month, then its average leaves that rating out.
Given a person who has not signed in, when they try to remove feedback, then nothing is removed.
Given staff press Remove, when the website asks them to confirm and they say no, then the feedback stays.
Given two members of staff remove the same feedback at the same moment, when both are done, then it is gone and neither sees a fault.

meaning.name: Ask after a purchase
meaning.statement: When a customer's order has been delivered, the website shall send them one request for feedback holding a link to the feedback page.

meaning.says: Given an order delivered on 3 March, when the delivery is known, then the customer receives one request holding a link to the feedback page.
Given an order for three products, when it is delivered, then the customer receives one request for the order, not three.
Given a customer the website has no way of reaching, when their order is delivered, then no request is sent and nothing else changes.
Given a request that cannot be delivered, when the website tries to send it, then the failure does not stop any other customer's request.

meaning.name: At most one request a month
meaning.statement: While a customer has received a request in the past month, the website shall send them no other request.

meaning.says: Given a request sent on 3 March, when another of the customer's orders is delivered on 20 March, then no request is sent.
Given a request sent on 3 March, when another of the customer's orders is delivered on 3 April, then one request is sent.
Given two of a customer's orders delivered on the same day, when both are known, then one request is sent.
Given orders from one email address on the online shop and on a marketplace, when both are delivered within a month, then one request is sent.

meaning.name: Email before text
meaning.statement: Where a customer can be reached by both email and text message, the website shall send the request by email.

meaning.says: Given a customer with an email address and a mobile number, when a request is due, then it goes by email and no text is sent.
Given a customer with only a mobile number, when a request is due, then it goes by text message.
Given a customer with only an email address, when a request is due, then it goes by email.

meaning.name: A link and QR code to print
meaning.statement: The website shall give signed-in staff a link and a QR code to the feedback page, to print on receipts and in parcels.

meaning.says: Given a member of staff who has signed in, when they open the printing page, then they can save the link and the QR code.
Given a QR code on a printed receipt, when a customer scans it with a phone, then the feedback page opens.
Given feedback sent from a printed link, when staff read it, then it reads and counts as any other feedback.

meaning.name: Opting out of requests
meaning.statement: When a customer opts out, the website shall send them no more requests for feedback.

meaning.says: Given any request for feedback, when a customer reads it, then it holds a way to opt out.
Given a customer who opted out on 3 March, when their next order is delivered, then no request is sent.
Given a customer who has opted out, when they open the feedback page by a link or QR code, then they can still send feedback.

meaning.name: When delivery cannot be known
meaning.statement: If the delivery of an order cannot be known, then the website shall send the request 7 days after the order was placed.

meaning.says: Given an order placed on 3 March with no delivery known, when 10 March arrives, then the customer receives one request.
Given an order placed on 3 March whose delivery becomes known on 6 March, when 10 March arrives, then the customer receives no second request.
Given a customer who received a request on 1 March, when 10 March arrives for an order with no delivery known, then no request is sent.

meaning.name: Delete after 12 months
meaning.statement: When a piece of feedback is 12 months old, the website shall delete it and the email address kept with it.

meaning.says: Given feedback that arrived on 3 March 2026, when staff look on 3 March 2027, then it and its email address are gone.
Given feedback that arrived on 4 March 2026, when staff look on 3 March 2027, then it is still there.
Given a customer who opted out on 3 March 2026, when their order is delivered on 3 May 2027, then no request is sent.

meaning.name: Keep every piece of feedback
meaning.statement: When a person sends feedback, the website shall keep it with the date and time it arrived.

meaning.says: Given feedback sent at 14:05 on 3 March, when staff look at it later, then it shows what was written and 3 March, 14:05.
Given feedback sent yesterday, when the website has been restarted, then the feedback is still there.

meaning.name: Requests and opt-outs per month
meaning.statement: The website shall show staff how many requests were sent and how many customers opted out in each calendar month.

meaning.says: Given 500 requests and 4 opt-outs in March, when staff look at March, then it shows 500 and 4.
Given a month with no requests, when staff look at it, then it shows 0 and 0.

meaning.name: No request lost to downtime
meaning.statement: If the website was down when a request fell due, then the website shall send that request once it is back.

meaning.says: Given a request that fell due on 3 March while the website was down, when it is back on 4 March, then the customer receives that request on 4 March.
Given a request that fell due while the website was down, when it is back, then the customer receives it once.
Given a customer who opted out while the website was down, when it is back, then no request is sent to them.

meaning.name: A record of opt-outs and permissions
meaning.statement: The website shall keep the date of every opt-out and of every permission to publish.

meaning.says: Given a customer who opted out on 3 March, when staff look at the record, then it shows that opt-out and 3 March.
Given feedback sent on 3 March with permission to publish, when staff read it, then it shows that permission and 3 March.
Given an opt-out from 3 March 2026, when its customer's feedback has been deleted after 12 months, then the opt-out and its date are still there.

meaning.name: Sign out
meaning.statement: When a member of staff signs out, the website shall show no feedback until someone signs in again.

meaning.says: Given a member of staff who presses Sign out, when it is done, then they see the sign-in page.
Given a member of staff who has signed out, when they press the browser's Back, then they are asked to sign in and see no feedback.

meaning.name: Read the feedback
meaning.statement: The website shall show the business's staff every piece of feedback they have not removed, newest first.

meaning.says: Given three pieces of feedback, when staff open the list, then all three show, the newest at the top.
Given no feedback yet, when staff open the list, then it says there is no feedback yet.

meaning.details: Each member of staff has a sign-in of their own. A developer adds and removes them, and the website has no screen for that.
meaning.name: Only staff read feedback
meaning.statement: The website shall show feedback only to staff who have signed in.

meaning.says: Given a person who has not signed in, when they open the address of the staff's list, then they are asked to sign in and see no feedback.
Given a wrong password, when someone tries to sign in, then they are refused and see no feedback.
Given a member of staff with the right password, when they sign in, then they see the list of feedback.
Given a member of staff a developer has removed, when they try to sign in, then they are refused and see no feedback.
Given repeated wrong passwords, when the limit on failed sign-ins is reached, then further attempts are refused for a time, even with the right password.

meaning.name: An email address for a reply
meaning.statement: Where a person gives an email address, the website shall keep it with their feedback.

meaning.says: Given feedback sent with ana@example.com, when staff read it, then they see that address with it.
Given feedback sent with no address, when it arrives, then it is kept and staff see no address with it.
Given an address written as ana-at-example, when the person sends it, then the website says the address does not look right and their words stay on the page.

meaning.name: A rating with the feedback
meaning.statement: The website shall let a person give a rating of 1 to 5 stars with their feedback.

meaning.says: Given a person who picks a rating and sends it, when staff read that feedback, then they see the rating with it.
Given a person who writes a message and picks no rating, when they send it, then it is kept with no rating.
Given a person who picks a rating and writes nothing, when they send it, then it is kept with no message.
Given a person giving feedback, when they pick a rating, then they can pick 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 stars and nothing else.

meaning.name: Satisfaction by month
meaning.statement: The website shall show staff the average rating of each calendar month.

meaning.says: Given two ratings in March, one of 2 and one of 4, when staff look at March, then its average shows as 3.
Given a month with no ratings, when staff look at it, then it shows no average, rather than zero.

meaning.name: Feedback per month
meaning.statement: The website shall show staff how many pieces of feedback arrived in each calendar month, leaving out those they removed.

meaning.says: Given 12 pieces of feedback in March, when staff look at March, then it shows 12.
Given a month with no feedback, when staff look at it, then it shows 0.

meaning.name: Permission to publish
meaning.statement: The website shall let a person say that the business may publish what they wrote.

meaning.says: Given a person who ticks the permission and sends their feedback, when staff read it, then it shows that it may be published.
Given a person who leaves the permission as it stands when the page opens, when they send their feedback, then the permission is unticked and staff see it may not be published.

speed
meaning.says: On a phone, the feedback page opens within 5 seconds, and Send finishes within 5 seconds.

meaning.name: capacity
meaning.says: The online shop platform takes under 500 orders a month today, so under 500 requests go out a month. How many there will be in a year has not been said.

meaning.name: availability
meaning.says: If the website goes down, it is back within one working day, and no request is lost.

meaning.name: security
meaning.says: The website uses an encrypted connection, never stores a password in readable form, and blocks repeated failed sign-ins. Only signed-in staff can see or remove feedback.

meaning.name: privacy
meaning.says: Feedback, and the email address left with it, is kept for 12 months and then deleted. What the law requires is asked in Q14.

meaning.name: accessibility
meaning.says: The website meets WCAG 2.2 level AA. Whether the law requires a standard is asked in Q14.

meaning.name: devices
meaning.says: The website works in current browsers on phones and computers.

meaning.name: languages
meaning.says: The website, its emails and its text messages are in English only, and its days and months run in the business's local time.

meaning.name: proof
meaning.says: The website can show the date of each opt-out and each permission to publish, for as long as each applies.

meaning.assumptions: That too little feedback arrives, that it is scattered and that it comes too late is the business's own experience, and nothing has been counted. The cheapest check is to count last month's feedback from each place it arrived. That the online shop platform can tell the website who bought and when an order was delivered is not known yet. The cheapest check is to ask whoever runs the shop (Q10).
meaning.name: Feedback website
meaning.problem: The business gets feedback from its customers by email and phone, in person, through surveys and forms, and through public reviews and social media. Too little of it arrives: most customers never say anything. What does arrive is scattered across those places, so nobody sees it all. It arrives too late: the business hears of a problem after the customer has gone. Nobody can see whether things are getting better or worse. This is known from the business's own experience; nothing has been counted.
meaning.release plan: Release 1, within 3 months: customers give feedback on the website, staff read it, and customers of the online shop platform are asked when their order is delivered. The printed link and QR code cover everywhere else. Later: requests for the business's own online shop and marketplaces.
meaning.summary: A website where the customers of a business that sells products give it their feedback. It is for those customers, and for the staff who read what they say. It lets the business know what to improve, catch unhappy customers, track satisfaction and collect testimonials.
meaning.users: The customers: people who buy products from the business, and who give it their feedback. They give it today by email and phone, in person, through surveys and forms, and in public reviews and on social media. The staff: the people in the business who read that feedback.
